title: Redo and front/back answer to the chords graphic editors use
detail: Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ are what a designer already has in their fingers. The redo audit found the opposite: Ctrl+Shift+Z would have undone.
check: pressed the documented chords with a selection made, and read the object order before and after each

title: An undo crossing an image no longer deletes it
detail: The image's persisted src was an object URL revoked at decode, so Fabric could not enliven it on restore and dropped the object — one undo deleted the asset. Revocation moved to session end. NOTE: the user later corrected the framing — the underlying complaint was that transformations never entered history, and this fixed the restore path rather than that. See vg-030.
check: imported an image, moved it, undid, and confirmed the image was still on the canvas

title: Entering a group makes only that group's objects selectable
detail: "You are inside a group" lived in grouping-manager's context array and only the layer panel read it, so the artboard contradicted the list. Worse, editor-shell routed every double-click into enterGroup, so double-clicking a text box to edit it recorded a group context.
check: entered a group and counted selectable objects: 1 of 51, where before it was 51 of 51

title: The trends chart is no longer the only aliased one
detail: MAX_BACKING_PIXELS clamped the largest chart to 1.53x while every smaller one got 2x, so the only aliased graph was the one a reader looks at longest.
check: compared rendered pixels per chart at equal scale; every chart now samples at the same multiple

title: An inserted object is named, and the name round-trips
detail: Without this, every object an author created was a uuid in the layer list, permanently.
check: inserted a shape, named it, saved the package, and read the name back out of the zip

title: The glass control renders on every object and says why where it cannot apply
detail: The user's own test found the first version incomplete: "The checkbox is unselectable but the tooltip only show when tabbed, not mouse hovering." aria-disabled rather than disabled, because a disabled control leaves the tab order and the reason would reach a mouse and nobody else.
check: selected a Line, tabbed to the glass control, and read what a screen reader announces: the control, and the reason it is unselectable

title: A bounded number field clamps onto its bound and carries a native slider
detail: "Took me a while to figure out blur only accepts 48 maximum." The field passed min: 0 and no max, so it had no slider and nothing to clamp onto. The user's first test said neither existed.
check: typed 60 into the glass blur field and read the field, the object and the new slider: 48, blurRadius 48, range min 0 max 48

title: Glass works on Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon
detail: Ruled by the user. Polyline, Path and Line are excluded — an open path has no interior to sample. A prior attempt to read this as "clamping proven nearby" is why the check names the shapes.
check: frosted a Circle, an Ellipse, a Triangle and a Polygon in the built editor and read each clip: the frosted patch follows the shape, not the bounding box

title: The player's failure screen names the cause, not a JavaScript parse error
detail: It printed V8's SyntaxError verbatim on a wall display, which is both meaningless to a reader and misleading — it says the theme file is corrupt when the likeliest cause is that nothing is serving.
check: pointed the player at a missing theme and read the screen: "The host did not answer with a theme — it may not be running."

title: A POSIX root volume joins its own drive
detail: library-devices stripped a trailing slash, turning / into "", and compared fs against mount. On Windows the path is C: and the strip is a no-op, so the suite was green and the whole platform was broken.
check: a test with a volume at / on a device that also holds /data; before, disk.total was undefined

title: A theme is a folder; a ZIP is only what an author exports
detail: Ruled twice by the user. The list() call was decompressing every package in the library to print N lines, and a 33 MB asset saved successfully and then 404'd. The window between two renames could also make a theme look deleted.
check: saved a theme from the real editor and read the folder: theme.json, assets/, thumbnail.png beside it

title: A saved theme can be read back by id
detail: Before, the editor could not open a saved theme at all: rename, save, reload /editor/, and the edit was gone. A save is a write-only surface with no way back to it.
check: renamed a theme, saved it, opened /editor/?theme=<id> in a fresh document, and read the saved name; a dead id falls back to the default

title: A stale save is refused rather than applied over someone else's work
detail: Two editors on one theme: the second save was built from a document that predated the first, and won silently.
check: three writes through the real API: current base 200, no base 200, stale base 409, and the stored theme unchanged after the 409

title: An unchanged save writes and uploads nothing
detail: documentKey boxed one JS number per asset byte and stringified it — 1,614 ms and 86 MB retained, on every open, new and save. The key now holds the envelope and each declared digest.
check: three saves of one theme with a 438 KB asset: the first request carried 1,169,576 bytes of asset data, the two unchanged saves carried zero

title: The two disk dropdowns stop asking the same question
detail: "Which device should dashboards use?" appeared twice, and the legend was the only thing telling them apart — and a legend scrolls out of view.
check: opened the two disk dropdowns on the settings page and read both prompts: they name different drives

title: The Arrange menu is gone; the toolbar above the canvas already had all eight
detail: Ruled by the user: the menu was redundant with the toolbar, not a drift to be synced. An agent was dispatched to make the menu offer all eight before the ruling arrived; it was killed with nothing committed.
check: read the menu bar in the live editor: File, Edit, Insert, View; the toolbar has 8 arrange buttons

title: A crop control is reachable for a selected image
detail: The crop manager was constructed, wired to history, and never called — 4.6 kB of tested code with no entry point. Found while correcting a claim about image history.
check: selected an image in the built editor, opened Crop, and read the session: aspect presets, Apply and Cancel

title: Delete removes an object from the collection that holds it
detail: canvas.remove searches canvas._objects, so a grouped child was never found — and the manager returned true and saved a scene identical to the one before, so nothing anywhere disagreed.
check: grouped two objects, selected a child, pressed Delete, and read group._objects: the child left

title: Reordering no longer moves a grouped object into the canvas collection
detail: All four ordering actions left the child in BOTH collections — same reference — so Fabric painted it twice and the scene serialised it twice. The binding is Ctrl+Shift+], not Ctrl+].
check: pressed Ctrl+Shift+] three times on a grouped object, then serialised: 51 top-level objects and the child once, not twice

title: The starter theme's charts render in the player, gauges included
detail: Fixed in 7904424 on 2026-09-28; what was missing was the evidence — the stack had never been kept. ECharts 6.1.0's _renderPointer reads _progressEls inside a data-diff callback assigned only after a render that drew an arc. Player-only: it renders before telemetry arrives and flips progress.show under a datum already present.
check: counted distinct colours in each chart own ECharts canvas on a real host: ram-gauge 6 to 57, vram-gauge 6 to 45, track ink flat

title: A selected Line shows a diagonal bounding box instead of two end handles and a rotate handle
detail: "A line should have two end handles rather than a diagonal bounding box" — corrected by the user to two end handles AND a rotate handle, because the diagonal box is what currently provides rotation, so end handles alone would leave a Line unrotatable. The diagonal box makes alignment and snapping useless and crops both ends when the border is thick. Fully specified in the plan at 41c208d; never built. Owner: controls-manager/renderers.ts.

title: Double-clicking outside an entered group does not exit it; only Escape does
detail: "double clicking outside a group didn't exit it, only the Esc key does." editor-shell.ts binds mouse:dblclick to enterGroupOnDoubleClick — enter only. Nothing on screen says Escape is the way out. Neither fixed nor recorded until the user tested for it.

title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: "they weren't being dimmed, which is the industry standard visual affordance that tells user they're inside a group." The layer list dims today (data-context="false"). The canvas dim was DECLINED, not forgotten: opacity is in Fabric's stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. This is a decision to revisit, not a bug to fix.

title: Locked and unlocked icons are hard to tell apart; locked should be a filled lock
detail: "Locked and unlocked icons in the layer panel is visually hard to distinguished. Locked should use a filled lock icon, not an outline icon like unlocked." The layer panel already has a KIND_ICONS pattern to follow. Small.

title: A locked object should stay selectable on the canvas, just not movable
detail: "Locked icon should still be selectable in the canvas, it just can't be transformed, moved. Otherwise user will have to go hunt for it in the layer panel." selectable: false is currently how a locked object is prevented from being transformed, and the same flag is what makes it unselectable — the same split the group fix made once.

title: The dirty guard fires on a freshly opened theme nobody touched
detail: "The dirty guard 'save changes before...' always fires, even on a newly opened theme that I haven't touched the artboard. Something must be polluting its save data, maybe the telemetry data is leaking?" CAUSE ESTABLISHED: two exports six seconds apart differ only in scene.objects.{17,18,44}.styles. removeRuntimeText rewrites a sampled reading's text to an em-dash but not Fabric's per-character styles array, which is not in SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES. A reading that changes length moves the spans, the serialised scene moves, the key moves. The user was right about the source and wrong about the mechanism. WANTS A SPEC, not a patch — see docs/product/../superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md for the adjacent question.

title: The drag-select marquee vanishes when the mouse pauses rather than releases
detail: "Drag to select overlay keep flashing during drag and disappeared when mouse stop (not released yet)." Almost certainly bound to pointerup rather than to the pointer that started the drag. Not yet measured.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: "The line chart animation is smooth most of the time but occasionally the whole chart will slide to the left for a short distance, like it's trying to correct a wrong position." CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED. Hypothesis class: a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change. Needs a measurement, not a guess.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: Asset handling: replace adds, the layer list is inconsistent, and some cannot be removed
detail: "asset should not be its own panel but folded into other places, replace doesn't replace but add a new assets, some assets show up in the layer panel some don't, some assets can't be removed, etc." FOUR defects and a placement question. (1) Replace allocates a new path per import, so it cannot be pointing at what it claims to replace — cleanest cause, fix first. (2) and (3) are one missing traversal, seen from both sides, and will mask each other. (4) waits on vg-034. #14 is this defect wearing one example.

title: A colour picker for paint
detail: The editor has no colour affordance at all; the palette manager's only control is free text. THE SEARCH ANSWERED THE WRONG ECOSYSTEM: @base-ui/react ships no colour picker, which is true and beside the point — the standing intent is Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind, and shadcn/ui has one. The alpha trap still binds: panel is #081523d9 at 85% and frost at 30%, so a bare input[type=color] cannot represent the part that matters.

title: A gradient editor sharing the colour picker's parts
detail: The palette accepts gradients — the Paint chooser offers Linear gradient, the manager has an angle and a stop list — but the stops are text fields. The reuse answer is that the colour picker's swatch and stop list already ARE the gradient editor: a solid is a single stop. Blocked behind vg-031.

title: The palette colour field accepts anything, and persists it
detail: rebeccapurple typed into the field is accepted with no alert and no diagnostic, written into theme.json, passes the published validator, and reopens. So the editor produces a file outside its own schema, and a valid CSS keyword renders document-wide. UPSTREAM OF vg-031: a picker does not fix this, because the write path does not check. A picker with validation still leaves free text unless the write refuses.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: "the glass blur strength on circle, it's way stronger than rect at the same value." RULING: a slight per-shape difference is an acceptable tradeoff rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. But that settles the acceptable case, not a bug under it — the working hypothesis is PARTIAL COVERAGE, where the sampled region does not cover the clipped shape and part of the Circle carries frost with no backdrop under it. A number says the region is already shape-dependent: the Circle's measured 127,449 px against the Rect's 156,009 for the same box, which a fixed padding cannot produce. Not dispatched — see issue for the state.

title: The crop notice contradicts the geometry it describes
detail: CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it is not the product's. The notice was right and my reading was wrong: .left and .top are the ANCHOR, not the box, and that theme omits originX/originY so Fabric revives it at originX center — the box runs -60.5 to 140.5 and the glyph run at -60.5 to -38.5, genuinely off a 1920 artboard. The real defect found alongside it is that a revived display had no artboard boundary at all, so objects painted over the letterbox bars while the notice said they were not shown. Fixed in 299c0bf.

title: Every unmatched host path serves the player
detail: server.ts:1017 falls through to the player bundle unconditionally, with nothing checking the path IS the player. /play and /display both return 200 with a live dashboard. An operator who mistypes a URL gets a working-looking display and no way to know the configured path is wrong — worse than a 404, which would have told them. Fix is one condition and a 404 the host already owns.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md.

title: A text object's Height field shows a stale measurement before the author has authored a height
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. Cause not re-established since.

title: A palette token added in the editor is keyed 'colour-3' beside a layer list that calls it 'CPU blue'
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. The two names for one token is the defect; the layer list is presumably the one a person typed.

title: A chart's series colours and its bindings are coupled by index, so removing a middle binding shifts the colours
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. A data-shape defect, not a visual one — a silent reassignment rather than a wrong colour.

title: A value run cannot be told not to print its unit, so a reading and its literal unit print the unit twice ("95.4%%")
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. Rendered output on the display's face, and the doubled percent is exactly the sort of thing a reader photographs and asks about.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: The background media is declared as an asset and has no layer
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. This is vg-030 for one specific kind of asset — the general case is filed, so this should be closed as a duplicate of it rather than tracked twice.

title: Delete cannot remove an object that lives inside a group
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry. FIXED in 82eef78 — see vg-018. Kept here so the issue and the registry agree; close the issue against vg-018.

title: The Ctrl+N discard prompt times out waiting for a Discard button
detail: Carried from the pre-GitHub registry, migrated 2026-09-27. Cause not established; pre-existing, and it is a test defect rather than a product one until shown otherwise.

title: The Performance Trends panel plots nothing while every other chart has values
detail: MEASURED, and not yet a finding. The preview source exposes latest() and history() as FUNCTIONS — an own-key on an object can be a function, which is how a first reading of history() as a field went wrong. Called properly after 5 batches and 7 seconds, history() returns an object with ZERO keys. chartPlaybackDelayMs exists on the same source, so playback may simply be slower than the window watched. Filed as a measurement with its method, NOT as a defect: this is the pass's most repeated mistake and a screenshot cannot separate an empty source from a broken one.

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.
